caption:
There has never been a better time to buy a watch in Japan. 

1. Low Prices
Thanks to a number of macroeconomic factors that started in the ‘90s, the Japanese Yen is really low. The watch market has not fully adjusted yet so you are able to find amazing steals. On top of this, in Japan 10% VAT is deducted straight from the price at the shop.

2. Large Vintage Market
Due to its economic prosperity in the ‘80s, Tokyo is the best vintage city in the world. Particularly if you take into consideration Japan’s attitude towards good maintenance. You will be able to find rare and unique pieces in amazing condition.

3. Watch Trends
Japan doesn’t always follow the same trends as the rest of the world as it can be quite trend insular. Popular watches abroad are still unwanted here and priced accordingly.

Most importantly just enjoy your trip and lose yourself in the experience.

Follow for my watch hunts and more!

Meat lovers save this post 🥩 Here are a few restaurants in Tokyo that you simply cannot miss. Follow @japanlikealocal for more or comment GUIDE to purchase our full list 🙌🏼

📍 Sumibi Yakiniku Nakahara - where the chef sources only the finest Japanese beef and grills it over charcoal. I know this sounds simple but trust me it will likely be one of the most memorable dining experiences you have in Japan. 

Average price: ¥20,000-¥30,000. Reservations are difficult to secure, often requiring months in advance. Try to get a counter seat! 

📍Narukiyo Tokyo is a quirky izakaya with achanging menu of seasonal dishes and phallic objects scattered around. It’s super fun and lively and it’s definitely one of those “IYKYK” places. 

Average price: ¥8,000-¥10,000. Reservations can be tricky due to its popularity and limited seating. As always, try to get a counter seat!

📍Sukiyaki Chinya - this is a traditional restaurant with over 140 years of history. Meat is sourced exclusively from Japanese Black Wagyu cattle and comes at a variety of price points. 

Average price: ¥12,000-¥15,000. Reservations are usually easy to make.

📍Akasaka Tsutsui is known for its beefsteak bowl that literally melts in your mouth. The restaurant has a a retro traditional Japanese atmosphere and decor and the food is very reasonably priced. 

Average price: ¥1,000-¥15,000. Reservations are recommended but not too hard to secure.

Let me know if this is helpful 😋
